newsitem.title: CHINA: China fines three firms for illegal share bid.
newsitem.headline: China fines three firms for illegal share bid.

text.p: The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has fined three stock brokerages for illegally using credit to bid for new share issues, the China Securities newspaper reported on Thursday.
One, the Shanghai branch of J & A Securities, used credit totalling 70.58 million yuan to bid for domestic currency A shares in Qinghai Mingjiao Co Ltd which were listed in October, it said.

The Shanghai branches of Shandong International Trust and Investment Co and Guangdong Securities Co, also used credit of 51.76 million yuan and 11.65 million yuan respectively to bid for Jiangsu Supu A shares, listed in August, it said.
China bans the use of credit to bid for new share issues, in part because it reduces the chances of smaller investors to buy them.
The CSRC has fined the three brokerages and given them an official warning, the newspaper said but gave no more details.
Last month the CSRC announced punishments for 12 financial institutions for illegal bidding for shares.
